title: VEX-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Assessing Exploitability of Software Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
abstract: arXiv:2609.08040v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The software supply chain has become an increasingly exposed attack surface because of its reliance on intricate yet fragile dependencies. Existing defenses such as GitHub Dependabot often raise many false alerts because their coarse-grained matching cannot determine whether a vulnerable dependency is actually exploitable. Security analysts typically spend substantial time assessing vulnerability exploitability case by case. Recent LLM agents have emerged as promising candidates for this task given their advanced capabilities in coding and cybersecurity, yet no existing benchmark evaluates them on it. Prior benchmarks target zero-day settings, where agents detect and exploit previously unknown vulnerabilities. translated_title: VEX-Bench：用于评估大语言模型智能体判断软件供应链漏洞可利用性能力的基准测试
translated_abstract: 摘要：软件供应链由于依赖复杂而脆弱的依赖关系，已成为日益暴露的攻击面。现有的防御措施（如 GitHub Dependabot）经常产生大量误报，因为其粗粒度匹配无法判断易受攻击的依赖是否真正可被利用。安全分析师通常需要花费大量时间逐一评估漏洞的可利用性。最近的大语言模型（LLM）智能体凭借其在编程和网络安全方面的先进能力，已成为完成这项任务的有前景的候选者，但目前尚无基准测试对此进行评估。以往的基准测试针对的是零日漏洞场景，即智能体检测并利用先前未知的漏洞。相比之下，软件供应链安全关注的是上游依赖中的已知漏洞如何影响下游项目，这要求智能体跨代码库进行推理，并判断上游漏洞是否能够影响下游项目。
tldr: 该论文提出了VEX-Bench，这是首个专门用于评估大语言模型智能体判断软件供应链中已知漏洞对下游项目可利用性能力的基准测试，填补了以往基准仅针对零日漏洞场景的空白。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces VEX-Bench, the first benchmark for evaluating LLM agents' ability to assess the exploitability of known software supply chain vulnerabilities for downstream projects, filling the gap left by prior benchmarks that only target zero-day settings.
